library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smith_2026_VRC07523LS"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smith_2026_VRC07523LS"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70488> (open access; Supplementary
  Appendix S1 carries Tables S1-S2)

VRC07-523LS is a CD4-binding-site broadly neutralizing anti-HIV-1 IgG1 with
the LS (M428L/N434S) Fc mutation that extends its half-life. Smith 2026 fitted
a two-compartment model with first-order subcutaneous absorption to serum
concentrations from adults without HIV and adults with untreated HIV-1
viremia, using a previously published VRC07-523LS model (Mayer 2024) as a
Bayesian prior. Clearance rises with the time-varying plasma HIV-1 RNA
through a hyperbolic function:

$$CL_i(t) = CL_{TV} \cdot \left(1 + E_{max,i} \cdot \frac{HIV(t)^\gamma}{EC_{50}^\gamma + HIV(t)^\gamma}\right) \cdot e^{\eta_{CL,i}}$$

with $\gamma$ fixed to 1. In the packaged model the viral load is the
covariate column `HIV_VLOAD` (copies/mL, linear scale); set it to 0 for
people without HIV or with suppressed virus.

# Population

The model was fitted to 34 adults (Supplementary Table S1): 25 healthy adults
from the VRC 605 phase 1 dose-escalation trial (NCT02840474; 1, 5, 20 or
40 mg/kg IV, or 5 mg/kg SC, as single doses or three doses 12 weeks apart)
and 9 adults with chronic HIV-1 viremia not on antiretroviral therapy
(NCT03015181), who received 40 mg/kg IV and started antiretroviral therapy
about two weeks later. Median weight was 75.1 kg (IQR 61.5-85.05), median age
26 years (IQR 23.25-31.75), and 44.1% were female; 26 participants (76.5%)
received IV and 8 (23.5%) SC doses. In the viremic group the mean viral load
was 35,264 copies/mL at antibody initiation, rebounded to a peak of 4,410
copies/mL at week 3, and was suppressed (mean 22.2 copies/mL) by weeks 7-8
(Figure 1).

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smith_2026_VRC07523LS"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: two-compartment, first-order SC absorption | -- | Results, first paragraph of "The Influence of Viremia on BNAb Pharmacokinetics" |
| `CL(t) = CL_TV * (1 + Emax * HIV^gamma / (EC50^gamma + HIV^gamma)) * exp(eta)` | -- | Results, clearance equation |
| `lka` (absorption half-life Tabs) | 2.02 day, ka = ln(2)/2.02 | Table 1 `T abs` |
| `logitfdepot` (SC bioavailability) | 0.486 | Table 1 `F bio` |
| `lcl` (CL without viral load) | 99.3 mL/day | Table 1 `CL` |
| `lvc` (V1) | 2080 mL | Table 1 `V1` |
| `lvp` (V2) | 2760 mL | Table 1 `V2` |
| `lq` (CLD) | 518 mL/day | Table 1 `CLD` |
| `le_vload_cl` (Emax, maximal fractional CL increase) | 5.46 | Table 1 `CLmax`; Results "increase to 5.46-fold higher (i.e., CL = 641 mL/day)" |
| `lvload50_cl` (EC50) | 10^4.22 = 16,596 copies/mL | Table 1 `EC50` (log10 copy/mL); Results "16,595 copies/mL" |
| `hill` (gamma) | 1 (fixed) | Table 1 `gamma` |
| `etalka` | 0.481^2 | Table 1 `omega Tabs` (SD) |
| `etalogitfdepot` | 1.06^2 | Table 1 `omega F` (SD) |
| `etalcl`, `etalvp` and their covariance | 0.296^2, 0.390^2, 0.819 x 0.296 x 0.390 | Table 1 `omega CL`, `omega V2`, `rho CL ~ V2` |
| `etalvc` | 0.382^2 | Table 1 `omega V1` |
| `etalq` | 0.611^2 | Table 1 `omega CLD` |
| `etale_vload_cl` | 0.448^2 | Table 1 `omega CLMAX` |
| `addSd` | 0.523 mg/L | Table 1 `sigma a` |
| `propSd` | 0.204 | Table 1 `sigma p` |

# Typical-value checks

The closed-form typical values follow directly from Table 1 and are checked
against numbers the paper quotes in the text.

```{r closed-form}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Smith_2026_VRC07523LS"))
th <- mod$theta
cl0 <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) * 1000 # mL/day
cl_max <- cl0 * (1 + exp(th[["le_vload_cl"]])) # mL/day, HIV(t) >> EC50
ec50 <- exp(th[["lvload50_cl"]]) # copies/mL

# Terminal (beta) half-life of the two-compartment system without viremia.
kel <- exp(th[["lcl"]]) / exp(th[["lvc"]])
k12 <- exp(th[["lq"]]) / exp(th[["lvc"]])
k21 <- exp(th[["lq"]]) / exp(th[["lvp"]])
beta <- ((kel + k12 + k21) - sqrt((kel + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * kel * k21)) / 2
thalf_beta <- log(2) / beta

checks <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "CL at saturating viral load (mL/day)",
    "EC50 (copies/mL)",
    "Typical terminal half-life without viremia (day)"
  ),
  Model = c(cl_max, ec50, thalf_beta),
  Paper = c(641, 16595, 36.3),
  `Paper source` = c(
    "Results: 'CL = 641 mL/day'",
    "Results: '16,595 copies/mL'",
    "Discussion: median terminal half-life 36.3 days"
  )
)
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  abs(cl_max / 641 - 1) < 0.005,
  abs(ec50 / 16595 - 1) < 0.001,
  abs(thalf_beta / 36.3 - 1) < 0.05
)
```

The 36.3-day figure is the median individual estimate in the study, so it is
compared with the typical value only approximately.

# Virtual cohort and simulation (Figure 3)

Figure 3 simulates single 1-hour IV infusions of 700, 1400 and 2100 mg under
seven static viral loads (0 to 30,000 copies/mL). The paper used 1500 virtual
subjects; here each of the 21 arms has 200 virtual subjects. The model has no
body-size covariate, so no demographic distribution is needed.

```{r fig3-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260211)
n_per_arm <- 200
arms <- expand.grid(
  dose = c(700, 1400, 2100),
  vl = c(0, 100, 300, 1000, 3000, 10000, 30000)
)
arms$arm <- seq_len(nrow(arms))
t_obs <- seq(0, 75 * 7, by = 1) # daily for 75 weeks

make_arm <- function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = arms$dose[i], rate = arms$dose[i] * 24,
    evid = 1, cmt = "central"
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = t_obs)
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$rate <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0
  obs_rows$cmt <- "central"
  out <- rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$HIV_VLOAD <- arms$vl[i]
  out$arm <- i
  out
}
ev_fig3 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(arms$arm, make_arm))
ev_fig3 <- ev_fig3[order(ev_fig3$id, ev_fig3$time, -ev_fig3$evid), ]

sim_fig3 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_fig3, keep = "arm", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(arms, by = "arm")
```

```{r fig3a, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
sim_fig3 |>
  filter(vl %in% c(0, 1000, 10000, 30000)) |>
  group_by(dose, vl, time) |>
  summarise(
    med = median(Cc),
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.1),
    hi = quantile(Cc, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  mutate(
    Dose = factor(paste(dose, "mg"), levels = paste(c(700, 1400, 2100), "mg")),
    `Viral load` = factor(vl)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, med, colour = `Viral load`, fill = `Viral load`)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(1, 10), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.01, 1000)) +
  facet_wrap(~Dose) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "VRC07-523LS (mg/L)",
    colour = "Viral load\n(copies/mL)", fill = "Viral load\n(copies/mL)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 3A of Smith 2026 (median and 10th-90th percentile band;
dashed lines at the 1 and 10 mg/L targets).

## Time to 1 mg/L (Figure 3B)

The time to target is the first daily time after the infusion at which a
subject's concentration is at or below the target. Subjects still above the
target at 75 weeks are counted as reaching it after the simulated window
(`Inf`), which keeps them in the upper percentiles.

```{r fig3b}
time_to <- function(time, conc, target) {
  i <- which(time > 1 & conc <= target)[1]
  if (is.na(i)) Inf else time[i]
}
ttt <- sim_fig3 |>
  group_by(id, dose, vl) |>
  summarise(
    t1 = time_to(time, Cc, 1),
    t10 = time_to(time, Cc, 10),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ttt_sum <- ttt |>
  group_by(dose, vl) |>
  summarise(
    t1_p10 = quantile(t1, 0.1) / 7,
    t1_p90 = quantile(t1, 0.9) / 7,
    t10_p10 = quantile(t10, 0.1) / 7,
    t10_p90 = quantile(t10, 0.9) / 7,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ttt_sum |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose (mg)" = dose,
    "Viral load (copies/mL)" = vl,
    "1 mg/L, 10th pct (wk)" = t1_p10,
    "1 mg/L, 90th pct (wk)" = t1_p90,
    "10 mg/L, 10th pct (wk)" = t10_p10,
    "10 mg/L, 90th pct (wk)" = t10_p90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Simulated time (weeks) by which 10% and 90% of subjects are at or below each target.")
```

The paper quotes the 2100 mg arm numerically: under no viremia the 10th-90th
percentile time to 1 mg/L is 35.4-62.3 weeks (Results; the Discussion gives
35 and 60.5 weeks), and at a static 30,000 copies/mL it is 7.59-18.7 weeks.

```{r fig3b-compare}
pub_fig3 <- tibble::tibble(
  vl = c(0, 0, 30000, 30000),
  Percentile = c("10th", "90th", "10th", "90th"),
  Paper = c(35.4, 62.3, 7.59, 18.7)
)
sim_2100 <- ttt_sum |>
  filter(dose == 2100, vl %in% c(0, 30000)) |>
  select(vl, `10th` = t1_p10, `90th` = t1_p90) |>
  pivot_longer(-vl, names_to = "Percentile", values_to = "Simulated")
cmp_fig3 <- pub_fig3 |>
  left_join(sim_2100, by = c("vl", "Percentile")) |>
  mutate(`Difference (%)` = 100 * (Simulated - Paper) / Paper)
cmp_fig3 |>
  dplyr::rename("Viral load (copies/mL)" = vl) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Time (weeks) to 1 mg/L after 2100 mg IV: paper vs simulation.")

stopifnot(all(abs(cmp_fig3$`Difference (%)`) < 20))
```

The paper also states that, without viremia, the 700-2100 mg doses keep
concentrations above the IC50 of 0.055 mg/L beyond 52 weeks; the simulated
median concentration at week 52 is:

```{r ic50}
c52 <- sim_fig3 |>
  filter(vl == 0, time == 364) |>
  group_by(dose) |>
  summarise(median_c52 = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
c52 |>
  dplyr::rename("Dose (mg)" = dose, "Median at week 52 (mg/L)" = median_c52) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(c52$median_c52 > 0.055))
```

# Regimen optimization (Figure 4)

The genetic algorithm in the paper chose doses so that the 90th percentile of
the trough concentration equals 1 mg/L. Without viremia the selected single
dose was 924 mg. The Results describe the target time as 52 weeks and the
Methods as 48 weeks; both are shown below. With viremia the paper fixed the
viral-load time course at the 90th percentile observed in the viremic
participants (Figure 1) and reports a single dose of 1955 mg, or 158 mg
followed by 68 mg at week 26.

The 90th-percentile viral-load curve is not tabulated, so it was digitised
approximately by the maintainers from the upper edge of the 90% band in
Figure 1 and interpolated log-linearly between the points below. This makes
the viremic scenarios illustrative only.

```{r fig1-vl}
vl90 <- tibble::tibble(
  week = c(0, 0.15, 0.3, 0.6, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.3, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 52),
  vl = c(45000, 60000, 35000, 10000, 1400, 7000, 9000, 9000, 14000, 7500, 700, 40, 25, 25)
)
vl_at <- function(t_day) {
  10^approx(vl90$week * 7, log10(vl90$vl), xout = t_day, rule = 2)$y
}
```

```{r fig4}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260212)
n_fig4 <- 200
t_fig4 <- seq(0, 56 * 7, by = 1)
scen_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  scenario = c("No viremia, 924 mg", "Viremia, 1955 mg", "Viremia, 158 mg + 68 mg at week 26"),
  viremic = c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE)
)
make_fig4 <- function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * n_fig4 + seq_len(n_fig4)
  doses <- switch(i,
    data.frame(time = 0, amt = 924),
    data.frame(time = 0, amt = 1955),
    data.frame(time = c(0, 26 * 7), amt = c(158, 68))
  )
  dose_rows <- merge(data.frame(id = ids), doses)
  dose_rows$rate <- dose_rows$amt * 24
  dose_rows$evid <- 1
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = t_fig4)
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$rate <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0
  out <- rbind(dose_rows[, names(obs_rows)], obs_rows)
  out$cmt <- "central"
  out$HIV_VLOAD <- if (scen_tbl$viremic[i]) vl_at(out$time) else 0
  out$scen <- i
  out
}
ev_fig4 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(scen_tbl)), make_fig4))
ev_fig4 <- ev_fig4[order(ev_fig4$id, ev_fig4$time, -ev_fig4$evid), ]
sim_fig4 <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_fig4,
  keep = "scen", returnType = "data.frame",
  covsInterpolation = "locf"
) |>
  mutate(scenario = scen_tbl$scenario[scen])

troughs <- sim_fig4 |>
  filter(
    (scen %in% 1:2 & time %in% (c(48, 52) * 7)) |
      (scen == 3 & time %in% (c(26, 52) * 7))
  ) |>
  group_by(scenario, week = time / 7) |>
  summarise(p90 = quantile(Cc, 0.9), median = median(Cc), .groups = "drop")
troughs |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scenario" = scenario, "Week" = week,
    "90th percentile (mg/L)" = p90, "Median (mg/L)" = median
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated concentrations at the Figure 4 target times; the paper's optimized doses put the 90th percentile at 1 mg/L.")

# The 90th percentile of 200 subjects is a robust quantile; a mis-transcribed
# clearance or volume moves it by far more than the 25% allowed here.
p90_924_wk52 <- troughs |>
  filter(scenario == "No viremia, 924 mg", week == 52) |>
  pull(p90)
stopifnot(abs(p90_924_wk52 - 1) < 0.25)
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4}
sim_fig4 |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(scenario, time) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.1), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.9), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 7, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~scenario) +
  labs(x = "Time (weeks)", y = "VRC07-523LS (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 4 of Smith 2026 (median and 10th-90th percentile band).

For the no-viremia 924 mg regimen, the simulated 90th percentile is close to
1 mg/L at week 52, matching the 52-week target stated in the Results (it is
still near 1.5 mg/L at week 48, the time named in the Methods). The viremic
regimens also put the 90th percentile near 1 mg/L at their target times, but
they depend on the approximate digitisation of the Figure 1 band and are not
used as a formal check.

# PKNCA validation (healthy-adult dose groups)

The healthy-adult single-dose groups of VRC 605 are simulated at the cohort
median weight (75.1 kg), 200 virtual subjects per group, with no viral load.
The IV infusion duration is not stated in Smith 2026; 1 hour is assumed, as
in the paper's own simulations.

```{r pknca-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260213)
grp <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c("1 mg/kg IV", "5 mg/kg IV", "20 mg/kg IV", "40 mg/kg IV", "5 mg/kg SC"),
  mgkg = c(1, 5, 20, 40, 5),
  route = c("iv", "iv", "iv", "iv", "sc")
)
t_nca <- c(0, 1 / 24, 0.25, 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 42, 56, 84, 112, 140, 168, 224, 280, 336)
make_grp <- function(i) {
  ids <- (i - 1) * 200 + seq_len(200)
  amt <- grp$mgkg[i] * 75.1
  dose_rows <- data.frame(
    id = ids, time = 0, amt = amt,
    rate = if (grp$route[i] == "iv") amt * 24 else 0,
    evid = 1, cmt = if (grp$route[i] == "iv") "central" else "depot"
  )
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = t_nca)
  obs_rows$amt <- 0
  obs_rows$rate <- 0
  obs_rows$evid <- 0
  obs_rows$cmt <- "central"
  out <- rbind(dose_rows, obs_rows)
  out$HIV_VLOAD <- 0
  out$treatment <- grp$treatment[i]
  out
}
ev_nca <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(grp)), make_grp))
ev_nca <- ev_nca[order(ev_nca$id, ev_nca$time, -ev_nca$evid), ]
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
```

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_nca |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- ev_nca |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "day")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

The only NCA-type quantity the paper reports is the median terminal
half-life without viremia, 36.3 days (Discussion). It is compared with the
simulated IV groups, whose terminal phase is not confounded by absorption.

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tibble(
  treatment = c("1 mg/kg IV", "5 mg/kg IV", "20 mg/kg IV", "40 mg/kg IV"),
  half.life = 36.3
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "half.life",
  units = c(half.life = "day"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs published median terminal half-life (IV groups). * marks rows differing by >20%.")

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life", grepl("IV", treatment))
stopifnot(abs(median(hl$PPORRES) / 36.3 - 1) < 0.15)
```

The model has linear clearance in the absence of viremia, so dose-normalized
exposure is the same across the IV groups; the half-life is close to the
published median in every group.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Scale of the bioavailability IIV.** Table 1 gives `omega F` = 1.06 (as
  an SD) without saying on which scale it acts. A log-normal eta of that size
  would give about a quarter of subjects a bioavailability above 1, so the
  model applies it on the logit scale (`logitfdepot`), which keeps F in
  (0, 1) with the typical value 0.486 as the median.
* **Other IIV.** All other etas are log-normal, as the clearance equation
  (`exp(eta_CL)`) shows for CL; Table 1 reports each omega as an SD, so the
  variances are the squares. The absorption half-life IIV is placed on
  `log(ka)` (`ka = ln(2) / Tabs`), which is the same distribution with the
  sign of the eta reversed.
* **Bootstrap column for V2 and CLD.** In Table 1 the bootstrap medians of
  `omega V2` (0.614) and `omega CLD` (0.387) look transposed relative to the
  estimates (0.390 and 0.611). The model uses the Estimate column.
* **EC50 scale.** Table 1 lists EC50 as 4.22 on the log10 scale; the Results
  give the same value as 16,595 copies/mL. The model uses the linear value
  10^4.22 in the hyperbolic function of the linear viral load. Applying the
  function to log10 viral load instead would give a large clearance increase
  at viral loads of 1-30 copies/mL, which the Figure 3 caption says were
  indistinguishable from no viremia.
* **Emax as a fractional increase.** `CLmax` = 5.46 is the increment added to
  1 in the clearance equation, so maximal clearance is 6.46-fold the baseline
  (641 mL/day), as the abstract and Results state.
* **Residual error.** Combined additive (0.523 mg/L) and proportional
  (0.204) error; the paper does not say whether the two terms add on the SD
  or the variance scale. The nlmixr2 default (variance scale) is used.
* **Supplementary Table S1 dose labels.** Table S1 lists the dose groups as
  "1 mg / 2 mg / 20 mg / 40 mg"; the Methods and the group sizes (3 / 11 /
  8 / 12) show these are 1 / 5 / 20 / 40 mg/kg.
* **Viral-load inputs.** The paper does not state how viral loads below the
  limit of quantitation were coded; at < 50 copies/mL the effect on CL is
  below 0.3% of Emax, so 0 and the limit give the same prediction.
* **Infusion duration.** 1 hour, as in the paper's Figure 4 simulations.
* **Figure 1 viral-load curve.** Digitised approximately; the viremic
  regimen checks in the Figure 4 section are illustrative.
* **Covariates screened but not retained.** HIV status, sex, height, weight,
  age, baseline serum creatinine and baseline hematocrit were tested and are
  not in the final model; they are listed in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **Participant-specific analysis.** The ADAPT5 maximum a posteriori fits of
  three ACTG A5386 participants (Supplementary Table S2, Figure 5) are
  individual Bayesian estimates, not a population model, and are not
  packaged.
